title: Update public docs + examples for tiered batching defaults (fast/standard/cost-efficient)
creator: Henry Cho
body:
## Context
Runtime-1.22 introduces workload-aware batching defaults with three customer-facing latency SLO tiers:
- **fast** (tail-latency protection)
- **standard** (balanced)
- **cost-efficient** (throughput/$ optimized)

We need public-facing documentation updates and examples so customers can:
1) Understand what changes when tiers are enabled / when they do nothing.
2) Pick a tier safely (esp. streaming vs non-streaming).
3) Override behavior correctly (route policy vs request parameter vs Dedicated tenant override).
4) Troubleshoot regressions using reason codes and Console/metrics.

This ticket covers **docs site** + **examples repo** updates needed for launch readiness.

## Goals
- Explain tiers without over-promising (focus on typical trade-offs and guardrails).
- Provide clear “default behavior” language (what happens if you do nothing).
- Provide practical guidance per workload: chat/agent streaming, doc search, summarization/batch, code.
- Provide an operator-grade troubleshooting checklist and escalation path.
- Ensure docs align with:
  - final tier naming decision (fast/standard/cost-efficient)
  - override precedence rules (Dedicated + route-level + request-level)
  - reason codes emitted by runtime
  - SDK ergonomics (Python/TS tier option + header)

## Deliverables
### A) Docs site updates (public)
- New page: **Batching defaults: SLO tiers**
  - What is tiered batching?
  - When to choose each tier
  - Streaming considerations (TTFT vs overall latency, p99 sensitivity)
  - Overload behavior (backpressure / admission control) at a high level
  - “Why did I get this tier/profile?” pointers (reason codes + Console)
- Update existing pages:
  - Hosted API “Performance / latency” section: add tier selection and default behavior
  - Dedicated “Configuration / overrides” section: add precedence and common pitfalls
  - FAQ additions (below)

### B) Examples repo updates
- Add an example showing:
  - selecting tier via SDK option
  - selecting tier via header (curl)
  - route-level default + per-request override example
- Add migration note: from manual batching knobs → tier selection

### C) Troubleshooting + support alignment
- Troubleshooting section that maps symptoms → likely causes → next steps:
  - fast tier p99 regression
  - cost-efficient tier increased TTFT
  - dedicated override not taking effect
  - dashboards show missing tier dimension / reason code
  - overload/backpressure errors

## Proposed doc copy (high-signal, minimal marketing)
### Tier definitions (customer-facing)
- **fast**: prioritize low tail latency under concurrency; tighter batching wait budget and stricter admission control. Recommended for interactive and streaming chat/agent endpoints.
- **standard**: balanced defaults intended for most production traffic; good starting point if you don’t have a strict tail-latency requirement.
- **cost-efficient**: allow more batching to reduce cost per token; may increase time-to-first-token and tail latency under bursty concurrency. Recommended for background jobs and non-interactive generation.

### Default behavior (must be explicit)
- If you **do not specify a tier**, Redwood uses the **service default** (initially: standard for most hosted routes) and may adjust internal batching based on workload signals.
- Selecting a tier **does not change**:
  - data handling / logging / retention policies
  - model output semantics by itself (though any perf changes can surface existing truncation/config issues; see troubleshooting)

### Override precedence (docs must match ENG-18430)
- Effective tier/profile resolution (highest precedence first):
  1) Dedicated tenant/cluster override (if configured)
  2) Route/model policy tier (Console / config)
  3) Per-request tier (SDK option / request header) *when allowed by org policy*
  4) Redwood default
- Note: some enterprise orgs may restrict per-request overrides.

## Acceptance criteria
- Public docs PR merged and deployed:
  - includes tier overview + selection guidance + FAQ + troubleshooting
  - includes explicit default behavior and precedence
  - includes at least one example per: curl, Python, TypeScript
- Examples repo PR merged with runnable snippet(s).
- Content reviewed/approved by:
  - Hosted API PM sponsor (Nikhil Sharma or Henry Cho)
  - SRE representative (Sean Gallagher or Aisha Bello) for troubleshooting accuracy
  - Runtime representative (Sofia Ivanova or Lena Fischer) for reason codes / behavior
- Links included to:
  - Console “effective tier” view (if available at launch) OR how to view reason codes via response headers/trace
  - metrics/dashboards name (public-facing reference should be generic; no internal dashboard URLs)

## Implementation plan
1) Draft docs page structure per docs IA (coordinate with Elliot Price).
2) Pull final tier language from customer messaging draft + tier naming email thread.
3) Add examples:
   - curl: request header for tier
   - python: `batching_tier="fast"` (or final parameter name)
   - typescript: `batchingTier: "fast"`
4) Troubleshooting section: align with runtime reason codes and common failure modes from canary threads/tickets.
5) Review loop + merge before staged rollout expands beyond hosted subset.

## FAQ (seed list)
- What happens if I don’t pick a tier?
- Can I change tiers without redeploying my app?
- Does tier selection affect logging, retention, or data processing?
- Why did latency get worse after choosing cost-efficient?
- Why does fast tier sometimes reduce throughput?
- How do I confirm which tier/profile is active?
- Can I set a default tier at the route level and still override per request?

## Notes / open questions
- Final public API for tier selection:
  - confirm exact header name and SDK param name before docs ship
- Console UX availability at runtime-1.22 GA:
  - if “why this profile” UI slips, ensure docs point to reason codes + support workflow instead
- Dedicated override restrictions:
  - confirm which plans allow per-request overrides when a Dedicated tenant override is set

## Links
- Confluence docs plan: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/public-docs-plan-batching-defaults.json
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/prd-batching-profiles-slo-tiers.json
- Release notes draft: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/runtime-1-22-batching-defaults-release-notes.json
- GitHub:
  - Docs PR: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-1882-batching-defaults-slo-tiers-docs.json
  - Examples PR: sources/github/redwood-examples/pr-402-add-tier-selection-example-and-migration-guide.json
  - SDK Python: sources/github/redwood-sdk-python/pr-1190-add-batching-tier-parameter.json
  - SDK TS: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-882-add-batching-tier-option.json

## Rollout coordination
- Docs must be live before:
  - Dedicated opt-in announcement
  - Hosted API default expansion beyond canary cohort
- Support readiness: coordinate with support playbook updates thread (eng/support channel); ensure troubleshooting section matches what Support will reference.
comments: 2026-02-06 (Wei Chen): Drafted outline for new docs page. Waiting on final header + SDK param naming so examples are correct. Looping in Henry Cho + Elliot Price for wording review.

2026-02-11 (Sean Gallagher): Please be explicit that fast tier uses stricter admission control under overload; customers may see 429/overload responses sooner instead of unbounded queueing. Add guidance on what to do (scale Dedicated / reduce concurrency / switch tier for non-interactive routes).

2026-02-18 (Lauren Bishop): Dedicated docs must include precedence examples. We’ve had confusion when tenant override exists and route policy looks like it should win. Please include a small truth table / examples.

2026-03-02 (Lena Fischer): Reason codes list is stable enough for docs as categories (default/override/model-constraint/overload-mode). Avoid enumerating every code string in public docs; those may change. OK to say “reason codes are exposed via tracing/headers” and link to API reference once finalized.
2026-03-19 (Wei Chen): Added troubleshooting checklist and included the ‘override not taking effect’ section based on SUP-48271. Requesting SRE sign-off on overload/backpressure wording.

2026-04-12 (Henry Cho): Please tighten language: no numeric p99 guarantees in docs; refer to tier intent + link to SLO tier page in product docs. Add doc-search and support-agent examples (streaming vs non-streaming).
2026-04-22 (Wei Chen): Docs PR (redwood-docs#1882) merged; examples PR (redwood-examples#402) merged; verified snippet compiles against latest SDKs. Ready for launch checklist.
